We ran the pilot in two classes at a private school north of Riyadh. The first group had 64 students, the second 59 after the Eid break. I measured scores before and after the dashboard rollout and recorded the delta per student. The mean difference was 6.2 points, lower than we expected. Three students dropped out in week three, two because their home internet kept failing and one transferred, so we excluded them from the analysis. Teachers opened the dashboard on 11 of the 30 days. I asked the supervisor why, and he said nobody had trained them properly. That is the main lesson: the tool did not fail technically, it failed because no one onboarded the users. We also found the Excel export lost Arabic diacritics in names with hamza, which took two weeks to fix. We could not measure long-term effects because the term ended. The practical takeaway is that daily usage, not tool quality, explains the gap between the two classes.
